assets.prompt: Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: production game animation sprite atlas with REAL transparent alpha. Input image1 is the identity/realism reference, input image2 supplies the approved rear-three-quarter batting stance direction. Preserve the exact same original adult Korean batter face, body proportions, gloves, ivory baseball pants, cleats, bat material and warm upper-left light. Change jersey to saturated clean ROYAL BLUE (#2455d6 family), helmet also ROYAL BLUE, with plain white piping. These blue material regions will be recolored in game; no blue in skin, gloves, pants or bat. NO logos, writing, sponsor, numbers. EXACTLY 4 COLUMNS and 2 ROWS, EIGHT equal SQUARE cells, landscape 2:1 atlas, generous transparent gaps between cells. One complete body in each cell; fixed scale, fixed pelvis anchor, soles grounded at 90 percent of cell height, entire helmet AND bat included within each cell with spare margin. Athlete height about65 percent of cell, allowing the whole extended bat inside the cell. All eight poses have the SAME camera, face, scale, full-body framing, and lighting. NO background, no floor/dirt, no baked shadow, NO checkerboard, no grid lines, no text. Strict animation continuity: row1 cells0-3 left to right, row2 cells4-7 left to right: (0) ready stance; (1) load weight onto rear leg with hands back; (2) small front-foot stride planting and beginning hip rotation; (3) accelerating bat rotation before contact, hands pulling through; (4) clear contact phase, bat extended forward through an imaginary ball at waist height; (5) follow-through across front shoulder with hips rotated; (6) complete balanced follow-through; (7) controlled return to ready. Anatomically correct shoulder/elbow/wrist joints, correct two-handed bat grip maintained throughout, two arms/two legs/no extra fingers; no floating or disconnected bat, no ball. This is realistic photographed/photogrammetric sports-player cutout quality, not illustration, not plastic toy. RIGHT-HANDED hitter, viewed from the catcher's position at a three-quarter rear angle, player occupies viewer LEFT side of home plate and watches the pitcher ahead to viewer right. Left shoulder/front leg point toward pitcher, hands at RIGHT rear shoulder, RIGHT hand above LEFT on handle. Bat extends toward viewer RIGHT at contact. Do not reverse handedness. Every pose faces same pitcher direction. Preserve actual right-handed mechanics.

Use case: photorealistic-natural. Asset type: game sprite atlas with real transparent alpha. ONE original adult Korean right-handed baseball pitcher, natural athletic anatomy, short dark hair, plain dark navy cap, navy jersey with ivory pants, black glove on LEFT hand and ivory/navy cleats. Match our baseball concept's premium sports-photographic skin/fabric quality and warm late-afternoon upper-left sunlight with cool sky fill. The camera is stationary at HOME PLATE looking straight at the pitcher, nearly frontal with slight three-quarter perspective. EXACTLY FOUR COLUMNS and TWO ROWS, eight equal SQUARE cells in landscape 2:1. One full pitcher per cell, identical identity/uniform/scale, body height65percent, plenty transparent clearance for full raised knee, glove, throwing arm and both feet, no clipping. Fixed imaginary mound ground baseline at90percent cellheight. Eight DISTINCT chronological frames read left-to-right then next row: 0 standing set position hands together at chest; 1 left knee raised in leg lift balancing on right rear leg; 2 striding left leg toward camera with hands separating; 3 left foot landing, right arm cocked behind head and left glove tucked; 4 right arm extending forward toward home plate at the precise release pose, baseball already left the fingers; 5 torso over front leg, right arm following through across left leg and rear right leg kicked behind; 6 recovery balanced over legs; 7 reset upright ready. Keep correct right-handed pitching mechanics, actual shoulders/elbows/wrists, no extra limbs, no floating glove, no contorted backwards knees. No baseball in flight anywhere on sheet: the ball is drawn separately by code. No logos, sponsors, words, numbers, scenery, mound, floor, shadow, checkerboard, separators, UI or watermark. Isolated transparent athletic cutouts, not a composite stadium shot or flat cartoon.
